name: BOLA on numeric/UUID object IDs
hypothesis: Example: BOLA on numeric/UUID object IDs — the dossier shows a matching surface (authorization); a controlled test with owned accounts/data would distinguish vulnerable from hardened.
test_sketch: Two owned accounts A/B. A creates object, captures its ID. B requests the same ID directly (GET/PUT/DELETE). Compare: 200 with A's data = broken object-level authorization. Also try IDOR via POST body id, X-HTTP-Method override, and .json suffix.
impact_hint: High — cross-account data disclosure, the most paid bounty class.

name: Role/plan restriction enforced client-side only
hypothesis: Example: Role/plan restriction enforced client-side only — the dossier shows a matching surface (authorization); a controlled test with owned accounts/data would distinguish vulnerable from hardened.
test_sketch: Replay a privileged action as a low-privilege owned account by calling the API directly (drop the UI gate). Watch for 200 vs 403. Try role param tampering (role=user -> role=admin) on profile-update endpoints.

name: Excessive agency — over-permissioned tools, no server-side authz
hypothesis: Example: Excessive agency — over-permissioned tools, no server-side authz — the dossier shows a matching surface (ai-llm); a controlled test with owned accounts/data would distinguish vulnerable from hardened.
test_sketch: Enumerate the agent's tools (function schemas, MCP manifests), then ask it to invoke a tool beyond your owned account's privilege (admin action, other-user data). If the tool executes, agency exceeds authorization. Grounded: OWASP LLM06 (2025, expanded for agentic AI) — "Keys to the Kingdom".
impact_hint: Critical — the model becomes a confused deputy with privileges.
